note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps.

steps.narrative: The Telegram capability receives the user text “turn on the light” and it enters the system through cap_im_tg_publish_inbound_text (cap_im_tg.c:252). That calls claw_event_router_publish_message("tg_gateway", …), which fills a claw_event_t — the fixed-size-buffer event struct (claw_event.h:18) with source_cap "tg_gateway", event_type "message", the chat and sender ids, and the text — and enqueues it into the router’s FreeRTOS queue. The hardware never sees raw IM bytes; the gateway’s only job is turning chat updates into events.
steps.representation:
Telegram update  ->  cap_im_tg_publish_inbound_text()   # cap_im_tg.c:252
  -> claw_event_router_publish_message("tg_gateway", chat,
                                        "turn on the light")      # publisher.h:19
  -> claw_event_t { source_cap="tg_gateway",                       # claw_event.h:18
                     event_type="message", chat_id=..., sender_id=...,
                     text="turn on the light" }
  -> FreeRTOS event queue
steps.title: Telegram message arrives

steps.narrative: claw_event_router_task (claw_event_router.c:2258) blocks on xQueueReceive(s_runtime->event_queue, …, 250 ms) and wakes on our event (:2266). It evaluates router_rules.json in file order against the match fields — event_type, source_cap, channel, chat_id, and text with exact or prefix matching. With default_route_messages_to_agent set (claw_event_router.h:38) and no rule claiming the message first, the unmatched text is routed to the agent: the rule action run_agent (CLAW_EVENT_ROUTER_ACTION_RUN_AGENT = 1, claw_event_router.h:57).
steps.representation:
claw_event_router_task()               # claw_event_router.c:2258
  xQueueReceive(event_queue, 250ms)    # :2266  <- wakes on the event
  for rule in router_rules.json (in file order):
      match? event_type=="message", source_cap=="tg_gateway"
  no match  ->  default_route_messages_to_agent   # claw_event_router.h:38
  action: run_agent                     # :57
steps.title: Router matches a rule

steps.narrative: claw_event_router_execute_agent_action (claw_event_router.c:1739) renders the rule’s input_json templates against the event context, builds a claw_agent_mgr_root_input_t with the flags PUBLISH_OUT_MESSAGE | PUBLISH_STAGE_MESSAGE | SKIP_RESPONSE_QUEUE | USER_INTERRUPT (:1779), and calls claw_agent_mgr_submit_root(&agent_input, agent_submit_timeout_ms) (:1795). Submission is asynchronous: the router moves on to the next event immediately. The reply will arrive later as an out_message event — the two halves of this trace are decoupled by the bus.
steps.representation:
claw_event_router_execute_agent_action()  # claw_event_router.c:1739
  input = render(rule.input_json, event ctx)
  flags = PUBLISH_OUT_MESSAGE | PUBLISH_STAGE_MESSAGE |
          SKIP_RESPONSE_QUEUE | USER_INTERRUPT   # :1779
  claw_agent_mgr_submit_root(&input, timeout)    # :1795
  -> request queued for the claw_core agent task
  -> router moves on (async; reply comes back as an event)
steps.title: run_agent submits to the agent loop

steps.narrative: The agent-loop task picks the request off its own queue and claw_core_build_iteration_context (claw_core_context.c:473) assembles the prompt: the configured system prompt, one appended section per registered context provider — memory profile, long-term memory, session history, skill list, capability tools — each logged as context_loaded … provider=%s context_kind=%s (:555), plus a “Core Request” section carrying the triggering Telegram text and source metadata, and messages[]. The tools[] array is serialized from the capability registry by claw_cap_build_llm_tools_json (claw_cap.c:337) in OpenAI Responses-API tool format — only LLM-visible groups (cap_lua, cap_files, …) reach the model.
steps.representation:
claw_core_build_iteration_context()   # claw_core_context.c:473
  system_prompt + one section per context provider
      (memory profile / long-term memory / session history /
       skill list / capability tools)  (context_loaded @ :555)
  + "Core Request": <telegram text + source metadata>
  messages[] = active user text + prior assistant/tool rounds
  tools[] = claw_cap_build_llm_tools_json()  # claw_cap.c:337
            -> OpenAI Responses-API format; LLM-visible groups only
steps.title: Context providers build the prompt

steps.narrative: The loop calls claw_core_llm_chat_messages and the transport performs a single blocking esp_http_client_perform POST of the full JSON body (claw_llm_http_transport.c:339) — no streaming; the whole response is buffered, then parsed. The LLM never runs on the chip: all backends (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, custom) are HTTPS clients, with presets like deepseek / api.deepseek.com / deepseek-chat (cap_llm_config.c:49). For “turn on the light” the model returns one tool call: lua_run_script with the light-switch skill’s script path and args.
steps.representation:
claw_core_llm_chat_messages()
  -> POST https://api.<backend>/... (full JSON body)
     single esp_http_client_perform, no streaming   # transport :339
  <- 200 OK, buffered JSON: tool_calls=[{
        name: "lua_run_script",
        arguments: { path: ".../led_strip_switch.lua",
                     args: { enabled: true } } }]
steps.title: HTTPS call to the cloud model

steps.narrative: The loop appends the assistant tool-call message and executes it against the capability registry. The descriptor with .id = "lua_run_script" is registered at cap_lua.c:683 and is LLM-callable. The runtime builds a Lua VM with luaL_newstate() + luaL_openlibs() and installs an instruction-count hook via lua_sethook(L, cap_lua_timeout_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, 100) (cap_lua_runtime.c:446), so the script cannot overrun its timeout_ms. It runs the exact script path the light_switch SKILL.md pins (SKILL.md:117). There is no human approval gate anywhere in this path — visibility gating in claw_cap is the only check.
steps.representation:
loop: tool_call_count > 0 -> execute against claw_cap
  lua_run_script({ path: ".../led_strip_switch.lua",  # cap_lua.c:683
                   args: { enabled: true } })
  -> Lua VM: luaL_newstate() + luaL_openlibs()
     + timeout hook lua_sethook(..., LUA_MASKCOUNT, 100)
                                                  # cap_lua_runtime.c:446
  -> script body: require("gpio") / led_strip ...   # SKILL.md:117 pins path
steps.title: lua_run_script runs the light script

steps.narrative: The script calls into the registered native gpio module — set_direction / set_level / get_level exposed by luaopen_gpio (lua_driver_gpio.c:73–83), which wraps the ESP-IDF calls (e.g. lua_driver_gpio_set_level at :52). gpio.set_level(pin, 1) drives the LED-strip pin high and the light turns on: “turn on the light” becomes a voltage on a wire. Hardware is reachable only through these registered native modules; the script cannot touch registers directly.
steps.representation:
Lua: gpio.set_direction(PIN, "output")
     gpio.set_level(PIN, 1)            # lua_driver_gpio.c:73 (luaopen_gpio)
  -> lua_driver_gpio_set_level()      # :52
  -> gpio_set_level(pin, 1)           # ESP-IDF
  => LED on
  tool result { ok: true } -> appended to messages[]
steps.title: GPIO flips the light

steps.narrative: With the tool result in messages[], the next iteration’s model call returns tool_call_count == 0, so the loop takes the finalize path (claw_core_agent_loop.c:332): claw_core_finish_from_plain_text, session context persisted, break. Along the way, stage notes were published per round and per tool call (claw_core_publish_stage_note_for_round, :334) — the “typing…” UX that keeps the Telegram user informed across the slow HTTPS round-trips. The hard cap (iteration >= core->max_tool_iterations, :412) was never hit.
steps.representation:
iteration N: llm -> tool_call_count == 0     # claw_core_agent_loop.c:332
  claw_core_finish_from_plain_text(...)       # :335
  persist session context; break
  (during run: stage notes per round/tool call  # :334
   -> Telegram "typing..." during slow HTTPS calls)
final text: "Done — the light is on."
steps.title: Loop finalizes the answer

steps.narrative: claw_core_publish_out_message_if_requested (claw_core_events.c:156) builds an out_message event via build_out_message_event_common (:62): source_cap="claw_core", event_type="out_message", session policy CLAW_SESSION_POLICY_CHAT, addressed to target_channel/target_chat_id with correlation_id set to the source message id — then publishes it with claw_event_router_publish (:173). The agent’s output is just another event on the same bus the Telegram message arrived on; nothing about the reply path is special-cased.
steps.representation:
claw_core_publish_out_message_if_requested()  # claw_core_events.c:156
  build_out_message_event_common(...)          # :62
  -> claw_event_t { source_cap="claw_core",
                     event_type="out_message",
                     target_channel="tg", target_chat_id=...,
                     correlation_id=<source message id>,
                     text="Done — the light is on." }
  claw_event_router_publish(&event)            # :173
steps.title: Agent reply re-enters the bus

steps.narrative: The router task wakes again, matches the out_message event to a send_message rule (CLAW_EVENT_ROUTER_ACTION_SEND_MESSAGE = 3, claw_event_router.h:59), and the outbound binding calls the Telegram sendMessage API (cap_im_tg_api_call("sendMessage", …), cap_im_tg.c:794). The user sees “Done — the light is on.” With the queue drained, the router task parks in xQueueReceive(…, 250 ms) (claw_event_router.c:2266) and the agent-loop task parks on its own request queue (portMAX_DELAY, claw_core_agent_loop.c:121) — the device idles on milliwatts until the next event.
steps.representation:
router: out_message -> send_message rule     # claw_event_router.h:59
  -> cap_im_tg_api_call("sendMessage", chat_id, text)  # cap_im_tg.c:794
  => user sees "Done — the light is on."
queues drain:
  router: xQueueReceive(..., 250ms)      # claw_event_router.c:2266
  agent loop: xQueueReceive(..., portMAX_DELAY)  # :121
  => idle (milliwatts until the next event)
steps.title: Reply sent; device goes idle
